purpose: Which real models actually go wrong when the config asks them to? Measured, not assumed. Every row is a real run at temperature 0 on the same fixtures.
preset: bugs/presets/loop.yaml — stop rule removed, explicit licence to keep searching, max_steps 40

results.note: Twice: 12 steps/23,136 tokens and 10 steps/15,478 tokens on separate runs.
Adds one extra search under the buggy prompt, then stops on its own.
results.run_variance: Two runs of the identical clean config gave 3 steps and 4 steps. Temperature 0 does NOT make a hosted model bit-identical; route/load-balancer variation is the likely cause.

Same pattern: +1 step, +409 tokens, still answers correctly.

DIFFERENT FAULT from the same model on groq. On groq the buggy prompt caused a 12-step overrun; on openrouter the run ended after ONE step because turn 2 returned neither content nor a tool call. Both are real model misbehaviour under the same prompt, but they are not the same bug, and the OpenRouter one exposed a defect in Medic: an empty response was being recorded as stopped_because=final_answer with an empty answer, so a genuine model fault read as a legitimate empty conclusion. Now reported as failure_type=other with stopped_because=empty_response.

finding: The buggy prompt reliably costs these models one extra search and 400-1,400 extra tokens — the budget pressure is visible — but none of them runs away. gpt-oss-20b is the only one that exceeds the step limit, by 50%. The SAME model name on a DIFFERENT host fails differently: 12-step overrun on groq, single empty response on openrouter.
interpretation: This is a capability difference, not a fluke. A model that keeps re-searching despite an explicit licence to stop has weaker instruction-following on termination. It does NOT mean the loop bug is fake: it reproduces on the one model tested that misbehaves, it reproduces deterministically with the scripted agent, and a real deployment would run a spread of models including weaker ones.
consequence_for_the_demo: The demo needs a genuine, REPRODUCIBLE failure. groq gives a 12-step overrun that is easy to show and easy to fix (6 steps after). OpenRouter's empty response is also a real fault but is a worse demo: it ends in one step, so there is no visible runaway behaviour, and it may not recur on every run. Use groq for the demo take; keep openrouter as the same-model fallback for when groq's daily budget is exhausted, and be explicit on camera about which provider served the run.
cost_of_this_choice: Groq's free tier is 200,000 tokens/day and a looping run alone costs ~23,000 of it. A single demo day of rehearsals could exhaust the budget. This is the single largest demo-day risk and is recorded as such.
not_measured: Whether any NaraRouter model reproduces bug 1 or bug 2 — not tested.
Whether the models above reproduce loop at other temperatures or on other tasks.
How many times each was run: one clean + one buggy run per model, except gpt-oss-20b which was run twice on the buggy preset.
determinism_note: Every model here was run once clean + once buggy, except gpt-oss-20b (twice on buggy). A repeat clean run of laguna-s-2.1 differed by one step, so any single-run figure here should be read as an observation, not a constant. The scripted agent IS deterministic, which is why it backs the tests and the backup demo.

verification_notes.slug_change: every ':free' slug on OpenRouter is retired - 404 'unavailable for free - use this slug instead'. The paid slug openai/gpt-oss-20b is required and was verified to emit real tool calls.
verification_notes.provider_attribution: An earlier 'openrouter' probe silently ran on groq: the chain skipped the unconfigured provider and fell back to the generic LLM_* provider, which is groq's. medic/providers.py now RAISES rather than falling back, because a measurement attributed to the wrong host is worse than none.
